selection.policy: aggregate counts, all failing lessons, one complete successful lesson per band

text:
# generator-shortcuts

**Strongest retained canonical-fitting rival:** leave rectangles with height
less than five or width less than five solid, and otherwise perform the
intended rectangle-relative checker erasure. Every supplied canonical rectangle
is at least 5x5. The declared rival fits all eight labeled records across the
two canonical variants, representing four unique inputs. This is an unshown
boundary extrapolation, not memorization of complete grids.

**Exact counterexample:** a 10x10 zero grid containing a blue (color 1) 3x3
rectangle at rows 4..6 and columns 5..7, using zero-based coordinates. Actual
Racket changes only its center `(5,6)` from 1 to 0; the rival retains 1.
The full input, actual output, rival output and hashes are in
`repo/generators/2bb81826c18d/counterexamples/thin_3x3.json`.

This was emitted by the original selected source at seed 5, sample index 0,
easy, with overrides `grid_h=10, grid_w=10, n_rects=1,
size_profile=compact, palette_kind=primary, edge_touch=False`.
The source hash is
`f4b85948212752aa24e5c08ff174cb850645663a6140f952eba2019154abf28b`;
the selected rule hash is `b0e1d6662c7a`. Public `arcpuzzles apply` executed the
saved input; the complete receipt and exact command are in
`checks/shortcuts/minimal_thin_apply.json`. The saved input must be used when
replaying this historical witness because version 2.1 changes seeded draws.

**Actual baseline teaching failure:** easy seed 2, start 0, no overrides,
three demonstrations plus one query. The rival fits all three demonstrations
and disagrees on four cells of a query rectangle. This was confirmed by both
public episode materialization and separate Racket application, with accepted
indices `[0,1,2,3]` and zero rejections. See
`checks/shortcuts/production_verified.json` and the retained task-owned
`counterexamples/baseline_ambiguous_lessons.json`.

**Does the proposal emit refuting cases?** Yes. Every default teaching slot
contains a lawful height-3 rectangle with at least two interior columns; its
canonical output differs from the thin-object rival. Two teaching slots in
each four consecutive raw draws distinguish all twelve declared rivals even
when one pair is withheld. The final real-production census checked 300
lessons / 1,200 pairs / 1,200 query rotations, with 1,196 unique inputs and
zero measured ambiguity, hook warnings or scoring/materialization errors.
The fixed-seed enumeration separately covered all four start residues in each
band: 12 lessons and 48 rotations. Exact final generator hash:
`2ce12fb99622a5ea1e7958e036849171fd84b8903f0a64e4e063a59dfaf58fff`.
See `checks/lesson-census-final.summary.json`, its full compressed companion,
and `checks/schedule-census-final.json`.

The additional canvas-column-phase rival fits the original three visible
demonstrations but fails a labeled canonical query, so it is deliberately a
LESSON_COMPETITORS member rather than a CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS assertion. All
conclusions concern the named rivals and stated populations; undeclared
rules, overridden lessons and universal identifiability remain outside scope.
